about: The MediaItem standard's _itemTitle rules, as cases rather than prose.
This file is the shared reference: go-mediaitems runs it, and the TypeScript and any
other implementation should run the same file rather than keep a second set of cases.
Non-ASCII is written as \u escapes on purpose. A file full of literal combining accents
is exactly the file an editor silently normalises, which would make the table agree with

sanitizeValue.note: a slash stands between words, so it is replaced, not removed
same
an asterisk decorates inside one word, so it is removed
the standard's own separator cannot appear in a value
unspaced separator; happens to give the usual spelling
leading dot stripped: it would hide the folder from ls, Finder and globs. The accurate rendering is a safeTitle of dothack
runs of - are NOT collapsed; only runs of space are. A title may legitimately contain --
Windows silently drops a trailing dot, which would leave the folder not matching its own _itemTitle
interior dots survive; only the trailing one goes

sanitizeValue.input: Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring, The
sanitizeValue.want: Lord of the Rings The Fellowship of the Ring, The
sanitizeValue.note: the standard's own worked example
colons are ordinary in game titles
removing the colon leaves two spaces, which collapse to one
angle brackets removed
Ed Sheeran's 2023 album. A leading - is kept: the standard reserves that prefix only inside MediaItem folders, and a MediaItem folder's parent is always an ItemType folder
_ becomes -, and the resulting leading - is kept
trimmed
TAB. A whitespace control becomes a space, NOT removed - removing it would weld the words
LF, same
NO-BREAK SPACE. Mapped before runs are collapsed, or implementations disagree about what counts as whitespace
IDEOGRAPHIC SPACE
LINE SEPARATOR
ZERO WIDTH SPACE removed: invisible, so two folder names would look identical and not be
BOM removed
RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE removed. This is the filename-spoofing vector: it makes a name display in a different order than it is stored
NUL removed
DEL removed; the old U+0000-U+001F clause missed it

REPLACEMENT CHARACTER kept. It means an earlier step could not decode the bytes, so the character that was there is already lost. Dropping it would give Bjrn, which looks like a plausible name and launders the corruption; kept, the damage stays visible. Warnings reports it
Persian with ZWNJ (U+200C) KEPT: without it the letters join and the word is misspelled
emoji ZWJ sequence KEPT: stripping U+200D would turn one glyph into two
NFD in, NFC out. HFS+ rewrites names to a decomposed form, so without a fixed form the same title gives folder names that do not match byte for byte
already NFC; unchanged

FULLWIDTH COLON survives on purpose. It is legal on every filesystem, and folding it would need NFKC, which would also mangle the full-width Latin that Japanese text uses legitimately. A homoglyph, not a hazard
idempotence: sanitizing an already sanitized value changes nothing

sanitizeToEmpty.note: nothing survives; Compose must reject this and name safeTitle as the fix

valid.note: a leading - is fine on a MediaItem folder
_ belongs to the suffix, which Valid does not take; use ValidFolderName
Valid asks whether the identifier CONFORMS, and the standard makes a reserved name a warning. ValidFolderName asks whether the folder can exist, and answers no
corruption is visible rather than blocking; Warnings reports it

warnings.note: a full-width colon, which looks like the ordinary one the rules remove
KATAKANA MIDDLE DOT, which resembles the standard own separator
beside Latin letters a joiner does nothing visible, so this looks exactly like SamSpade
the same joiner between Persian letters is doing its job; no warning
an emoji sequence held together by a joiner; no warning

warnings.input: Lord of the Rings The Fellowship of the Ring, The · 2001
warnings.note: an ordinary title warns about nothing
not a reserved name once the replacement character is part of it

validFolderName.input: Lord of the Rings The Fellowship of the Ring, The · 2001
Lord of the Rings The Fellowship of the Ring, The · 2001_tt0120737

validFolderName.note: a suffix value is whatever field the cataloguer found distinguishing
path safety applies to the WHOLE string, suffix included. Ignoring the suffix for conformance must never mean joining it unchecked
Windows reserves this for a device, so the folder cannot exist there and the storage unit stops being portable
the reservation is the WHOLE name, so a suffix that happens to be one is fine
a device name as a word in a title is fine

pathSafe.note: PathSafe is the security floor only. A reserved name cannot be a folder on Windows, which is ValidFolderName's business, not this one
a hidden folder is a conformance problem, not a traversal one
a profile slug, which is deliberately not held to the standard's rule
a backslash, which is a separator on Windows
a control character is never safe in a name, whatever else is true of it

validSafe.note: the case the field exists for
ZWNJ, so a Persian safeTitle can be spelled correctly
the separator is not allowed in a value, safe or not

sameName.note: Windows and macOS see one folder here, Linux sees two

reserved.note: a validator warning, not an error
the reservation is the whole name, so an ordinary title containing it is fine
Windows ignores trailing dots when matching
